explanation: Royal Navy officer Francis Beaufort drew it up in 1805 to judge wind by its effect on a warship's sails. Later versions describe waves at sea and trees on land instead.

claims.text: The Beaufort scale describes wind strength from force 0 (calm) to force 12 (hurricane force).
The Richter scale measures earthquakes, the Mohs scale mineral hardness and the Fujita scale tornado damage.
Francis Beaufort, an officer of the Royal Navy, devised the scale in 1805.
Beaufort's original scale judged the wind by its effect on a sailing warship's sails.
Later versions of the scale describe the wind's effects on the sea and on trees and objects on land.
